public_rationale: o3 was released in April 2025. OpenAI reported near-perfect scores on AIME 2025 competition math with tools, 98.4% pass@1. But OpenAI's system card found that o3 hallucinated more than o1 on factual questions about people. OpenAI later found that o3 gave confident answers about images that did not exist 86.7% of the time. So its reliability clearly varied by type of problem, as he wagered.
limitations: The forecast is hedged and 'reliable' is undefined, so the result depends on reading it as 'strong on some tasks, unreliable on others'.
The evidence is mostly OpenAI's own evaluations.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: once people can test o3, it will not prove reliable across the board. Its reliability will vary by type of problem, and 'at best' it will be strong on some types and weak on others.
No deadline was stated. The forecast settles once o3 is public and documented evaluations show its reliability by task type.
Strong performance on well-defined math tasks, alongside high error or hallucination rates on factual or other tasks, would match the forecast.

criteria.contradiction_condition: After release, evaluations show o3 reliable across a broad range of problem types, with no domain where it is clearly unreliable.
